page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The server is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by bottom-25% results in stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core tests, alongside poor single-threaded gzip compression. However, the instance leverages its 16 dedicated cores to deliver average multi-core performance across stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU benchmarks. Memory bandwidth is stable, with cached read speeds reaching 657.2 GB/sec and uncached read/write speeds performing in the average tier.

Given its high memory density relative to processing power, the ecs.se1.4xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-threaded compute performance. It is well-suited for database operations, Redis caching layers, and multi-threaded data processing tasks like bzip3 decompression. It can also handle moderate web serving and small-to-medium scale LLM inference, though it is not recommended for compute-heavy single-threaded tasks or workloads requiring local NVMe storage.
